title: JSON schema for lightweight unions, runtime validation, and user-friendly repair hints
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Tool/function calling currently uses full JSON Schema in model manifests which produces brittle runtime validation failures for 'union' parameter shapes (oneOf/anyOf) and confusing error messages surfaced to integrators. We need a lightweight, opinionated schema extension and a runtime mapping that: 1) makes union shapes predictable at validation time, 2) returns actionable repair hints (human-friendly) when requests fail, and 3) supports graceful coercion modes for host SDKs.

Goal: Define a compact, versioned JSON-schema dialect (+ conventions) for function/tool parameters that reduces false negatives during validation, unambiguously selects union branches via discriminators, and provides opt-in repair hints returned in the error payload and developer console. This ticket captures the format proposal, required runtime validation behavior, error codes, UX strings for repair hints, and an implementation plan for runtime-2.4.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc published in Confluence with examples for common union patterns (tagged unions, positional unions, property-polymorphic unions)
Runtime implements schema parsing and validation with deterministic union resolution algorithm and three coercion modes: strict, permissive, hint-only
Errors use stable error codes (RS_* prefix) and include a 'repair_hints' field when applicable
SDKs (python/js) demonstrate repair hints surfaced as structured suggestions (link to sample PRs)
No regressions on existing tool manifests: run validation test suite and ensure compatibility with legacy schemas using 'compat_mode' flag
spec: Overview: introduce 'rws_schema' versioned field for manifests that augments json-schema draft-07 with a small set of refinements: 'discriminator', 'preferred_branch', and 'coercion'.

Key refinements:
- discriminator: string | object path pointing to a top-level property to deterministically pick a union branch.
- preferred_branch: optional string hint used when multiple branches match to prefer one for suggestion-only mode.
- coercion: enum('strict','permissive','hint-only') controlling runtime repair behavior.

Union resolution algorithm (runtime):
1) If discriminator present and value matches a branch name -> select branch.
2) Else run a fast structural match on branches: exact match counts + required field coverage.
3) If ambiguous and preferred_branch present -> pick preferred.
4) If still ambiguous -> do not auto-coerce in strict mode; in permissive mode attempt best-effort coercion; in hint-only return repair_hints without coercion.

Error/response contract (HTTP 400):
- error_code: string (e.g., RS_TYPE_MISMATCH, RS_MISSING_REQUIRED, RS_AMBIGUOUS_UNION)
- message: human readable summary
- invalid_path: JSON Pointer(s) to failing locations
- repair_hints: list of short human instructions or suggested corrected payload snippets (stringified JSON)
- docs_url: link to a manifest-specific troubleshooting page

Backwards compatibility: add 'compat_mode' boolean in manifest. When true, runtime falls back to legacy validator (full jsonschema) and includes a migration_report if the new validator would have changed behavior.
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (design + tests): produce canonical confluence page and a suite of parametrized unit tests for union resolution (20+ cases)
Phase 2 (runtime): add 'rws_schema' parser in validator module, implement discriminator and matching flow. Expose coercion modes via per-route config and tenant override.

Phase 3 (SDK + UX): update Python/JS SDKs to supply permissive coercion by default in dev mode and surface repair_hints in exception objects. Console should display repair hints inline with manifest docs.
Telemetry: add metrics for RS_* error rates, counts of hint-accepted corrections, and percent of ambiguous unions encountered per model/route.
Performance: structural match must be cheap — implement short-circuiting heuristics (required fields count, simple type checks) and cap branch checks to 8 branches to avoid O(n) blowup.
Security: do not include secrets in repair_hints; redact values longer than 256 characters and mark as '<redacted>' in suggestions.
migration_plan: Communicate new 'rws_schema' in release notes and manifest authoring docs.
Provide a linting CLI that checks existing manifests and emits a migration_report with suggested 'discriminator' placements and 'preferred_branch' hints.
Opt-in rollout: enable new validator for internal staging tenants then 50% of hosted traffic with fallback via 'compat_mode' flag.
Create small incentive: display 'Detected: potential ambiguous unions' banner in Console for routes that would benefit from adding discriminators.
test_plan: Unit tests: 40 tests covering discriminators, ambiguous branches, permissive coercions, and redaction rules.
Integration: run full regression against 150 canonical manifests from production to detect behavior deltas.
End-to-end: SDK examples that show repair_hints surfaced as exceptions and a Console view that displays repair suggestions inline.
Load: ensure validator path adds <1% p50 latency for common request sizes (<=2KB payloads).
rollforward: If permissive coercions cause incorrect tool calls, immediately disable permissive mode for affected tenants and require explicit 'coercion=permissive' opt-in.
Quick hotfix: add server-side feature flag to revert to legacy validator globally.
Run postmortem and update migration linting rules to detect the problematic manifest pattern.
comments: 2026-02-12 - Aisha Kumar: Initial ticket created after spike showed 12% of function call failures were union-related and produced low-signal errors in Console.

2026-02-20 - Marcus Lee: Prototype runtime matcher added to branch eng/union-matcher. Basic discriminator handling implemented; still need coercion modes and SDK exposure. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428

2026-02-27 - Evelyn Park (Design review): Reviewed repair_hints UX. Recommended short (<=120 char) suggestions + an expandable example payload. Asked to avoid overwhelming Console with too many suggestions.
2026-03-03 - Security team (note): Confirmed redaction rule approach; metrics approved. Recommended review of telemetry sampling before GA.

2026-03-08 - Marcus Lee: Added unit test matrix and found three manifest edge cases where preferred_branch contradicts discriminator. Decided to make discriminator authoritative and preferred_branch only a tie-breaker in hint-only mode.
2026-03-10 - Aisha Kumar: Updated acceptance criteria to require manifest linter CLI tool and added due_date.
